digest.top_line: TNTCRT: 3yr DFS 74.8% v 66.0%, HR 0.674 (0.489-0.929) for doublet-LC TNT, with LRR ~6% in both arms so the gain is chemo, not RT.
digest.tldr: Rectal owns the day, and both TNT trials leave the RT question open in different ways: TNTCRT holds LCRT constant across arms (locoregional failure 6.03% v 6.19%), so its DFS/MFS win is chemo intensity and sequencing; STELLAR swaps 50 Gy/25 fx for 5x5Gy and clears DFS noninferiority (HR 0.883) at double the acute G3-5 toxicity (26.5% v 12.6%). Prostate contributes imaging-only signal: PSMA PET response and BCR natural-history data are prognostic, not yet a trigger for salvage RT timing.

sites.intro: Both entries are PSMA PET imaging arguments rather than treatment trials; neither yet tells you when to fire salvage or metastasis-directed RT.

studies.name: USPCC 2026 Point-Counterpoint: PSMA PET as Response Assessment
studies.tldr: Point-counterpoint arguing PSMA uptake is AR-regulated, so post-treatment change may track signaling, not tumor burden.
details: 🔍 USPCC 2026 point-counterpoint session, Steven Rowe (UT Southwestern); position: PSMA PET has no role at present as response assessment
🔍 Core argument: PSMA expression is dynamically regulated by the androgen axis, not a static marker of tumor burden
📊 Zukotynski J Nucl Med 2021: prospective single-arm 18F-DCFPyL PET/CT before and 2-4mo after abiraterone/enzalutamide, 16 evaluable pts
📊 Cohort-wide median time to therapy change 9.6mo (95% CI 6.9-14.2); median OS 28.6mo (95% CI 18.3-NA)

details.text: 📊 Zukotynski outcomes by δ-SUVmax response pattern (low vs high)

details: ⚠️ n=16 evaluable, single-arm, wide CIs (DASM HR 9.31, 1.81-47.87); prognostic separation, not validated response criteria
📊 Markowski J Nucl Med 2021: 6 men on bipolar androgen therapy, PSMA PET at baseline + 3mo; 3 progressed on imaging, detected earlier than conventional imaging
🔍 Repeatability data reviewed (Bland-Altman, ICC, within-subject CV) across SUVmax, SUVmean, SUVtotal, tumor volume; no repeatability values given in source

🔗 RECIP 1.0 (Gafita, J Nucl Med 2022) named as the emerging PSMA PET response framework for radioligand therapy, integrating PET with CT; presenter flags it as needing further validation before routine use
studies.significance: PSMA uptake falling after ADT or an ARSI can reflect AR signaling change rather than tumor kill, which matters wherever a post-treatment PSMA PET drives an RT decision: metastasis-directed SBRT target selection, or calling in-field response after treatment. Timing relative to systemic therapy start is the gating variable, and RECIP 1.0 is validated for radioligand therapy, not for RT response.
studies.monday_clinic: In APMR prostate cancer starting or on an ARSI, this argues against using a serial PSMA PET change alone to call response or trigger a therapy switch; it does not address PSMA PET for staging or for target selection in an untreated pt.

significance_by_specialty.radonc: A post-ARSI PSMA PET used to pick SBRT targets or to call in-field response can mislead: uptake tracks AR signaling, and the source gives no data on PSMA PET after radiotherapy at all. Scan timing relative to systemic-therapy start gates the read.
significance_by_specialty.medonc: For a pt starting abiraterone or enzalutamide, a rising or mixed uptake pattern at 2-4mo carried shorter time to therapy change (6.5 vs 12.2mo) and OS (17.8 vs 37.2mo), but from 16 pts. Prognostic, not a validated switch trigger.

open_questions: Kinetics of androgen-axis effects on PSMA expression
Repeatability thresholds for serial quantitative PSMA PET

studies.name: PSMA-Positive BCR Natural History Study
studies.tldr: Baseline data, first 130 pts: most BCR men with PSA DT >9-12mo still show PSMA-PET findings at PSA >5.
details: 🔍 Prospective NCI natural-history cohort; PSMA-positive BCR after definitive therapy incl. salvage RT (or declined it)
🔍 Eligibility gate: PSA ≥0.5 for baseline PET; negative baseline PET → annual imaging, any finding (even equivocal) → q6mo
📊 Baseline read of first 130 pts: PSMA-PET findings vs PSA doubling time at a single timepoint
📊 Vast majority of slow-DT pts (PSA DT >9mo, >12mo) had PSMA-PET findings once PSA >5
📊 Sites described: nodal disease, prostate-bed recurrence, small questionable bone lesions
💊 Therapy investigator-choice, not mandated; anything <6mo allowed (intermittent ADT, SBRT, intermittent ARPI, Radium-223 trials)
📊 Only ~1/3 have gone on therapy so far; majority observed off treatment
📊 Companion analysis (Madan, ~1.5yr f/u, first ~150 pts): 5 with conventional-imaging progression; >95% without abrupt PET change beyond what PSA DT predicted
⚠️ Baseline cross-sectional data only; median f/u ~2yr, interim outcome data not yet reported
⚠️ No effect size, no HR, no comparator reported in source; percentages other than ">95%" and "about a third" not quantified
⚠️ Single-institution NCI cohort with trial-enriched population (concurrent intermittent-therapy protocols) limits generalizability

verdict.rationale: Single-arm observational cohort, baseline timepoint only, non-mandated therapy, median f/u ~2yr with outcome data unreported. Descriptive counts, no comparator or effect size.
verdict.audience: PSMA-positive BCR prostate ca after definitive therapy ± salvage RT, PSA ≥0.5

studies.significance: The RT-relevant read is that prostate-bed recurrence and nodal disease turn up on PET in men with PSA DT >9-12mo once PSA exceeds 5, the exact group historically watched. That reframes who gets referred for metastasis-directed SBRT versus observed, but with only a baseline snapshot the cohort cannot yet say which PET pattern justifies treating.
studies.monday_clinic: In post-salvage-RT BCR with slow PSA doubling time and PSMA findings, this supports observation as a defensible option pending outcome data; it does not address men with rapid doubling time or conventional-imaging metastases.

analysis_sections.label: Design
analysis_sections.body: Prospective **natural history** observational cohort at NCI, ongoing, presented at **GU-ASCO 2026**. Reported analysis is the **baseline timepoint of the first 130 pts**; overall median follow-up is about **2 years**, with interim follow-up data still being analyzed.

analysis_sections.label: Population & inclusion
analysis_sections.body: Men with **biochemical recurrence after definitive therapy**, including those who already had **salvage radiation** or declined it. Entry requires **PSA ≥0.5** for the baseline PSMA PET.

analysis_sections.label: Regimen
analysis_sections.body: No mandated therapy. Pts may be **off treatment** or receive any therapy lasting **under six months**, including intermittent ADT, SBRT, and concurrent intermittent ARPI or Radium-223 protocols. Only **about a third** have started therapy; the majority are observed.

analysis_sections.label: Endpoints
analysis_sections.body: Descriptive: relationship between **PSMA PET findings and PSA doubling time** at baseline. Imaging cadence is protocolized, **annual** if the baseline PET is negative and **every six months** if anything, even equivocal, is seen.

analysis_sections.label: Results
analysis_sections.body: Among slow-doubling-time pts (**DT >9mo and >12mo**), the **vast majority** had PSMA PET findings once **PSA was above 5**: nodal disease, prostate-bed recurrence, and small equivocal bone lesions. In the companion ~1.5-year follow-up of roughly **150 pts**, **5** progressed on conventional imaging and **over 95%** had no abrupt PET change beyond what PSA kinetics predicted.

analysis_sections.label: Applies to
analysis_sections.body: Represents PSMA-positive BCR after definitive therapy with prior or declined salvage RT, PSA ≥0.5. Does not represent conventionally metastatic disease or men who would have been eligible for mCSPC trials on conventional imaging.

analysis_sections.label: Limitations
analysis_sections.body: Cross-sectional baseline only, so the reassuring stability claim rests on a separate smaller poster rather than this analysis. Denominators for the PET-positive fraction by doubling-time stratum are not reported in the source, and concurrent intermittent-therapy protocols at the same center may select a trial-willing cohort.

analysis_sections.label: Discussion
analysis_sections.body: The framing argument is that PSMA-positive BCR is a **distinct disease state**, not early mCSPC, and that treating it with doublet or triplet mCSPC approaches risks **overtreatment** in men who historically went years without conventional metastases. The cohort's purpose is to build the risk stratification that would license observation.

significance_by_specialty.radonc: Prostate-bed recurrence and nodal disease show up on PET in slow-DT men (DT >9mo, >12mo) once PSA passes 5, which is precisely the population previously offered observation after salvage RT. That governs whether a PET finding triggers metastasis-directed SBRT; the protocol allows SBRT but mandates nothing, so the cohort describes practice rather than testing it.
significance_by_specialty.medonc: About a third started therapy and the rest are observed, with 5 of roughly 150 progressing on conventional imaging at ~1.5 years. The read is against reflexive doublet or triplet mCSPC therapy for a PET-only finding, keeping intermittent ADT or ARPI as an option gated on PSA kinetics rather than scan positivity alone.

open_questions: Which PSMA PET patterns justify treatment vs observation
Whether PET progression precedes or tracks PSA doubling time
Durability of observation in PSMA-positive BCR

sites.intro: Two phase III TNT trials from the same era, one keeping long-course CRT and intensifying chemo, one shortening RT to 5x5Gy: local control is already ~94% in both, so RT's remaining lever is fractionation and toxicity, not dose.

studies.name: TNTCRT
studies.tldr: 3yr DFS 74.8% v 66.0%, HR 0.674 (0.489-0.929), P=.016 favoring doublet-LC TNT over nCRT in high-risk LARC.
details: 🔍 Phase III multicenter RCT, N=458 (232 doublet-LC TNT v 226 nCRT), enrolled 6/2017-12/2023, median f/u 51mo
🔍 Eligibility: stage II/III LARC, age 18-70, ≥1 MRI high-risk feature (cT4a-b, cN2, MRF+, or cT3c-d with EMVI)
💊 TNT arm: 1 cycle induction CAPOX → LCRT with 2 cycles concurrent CAPOX → 3 cycles consolidation CAPOX → surgery
💊 Control: LCRT with concurrent capecitabine → surgery → 6 cycles adjuvant CAPOX starting 4-8wk post-op
📐 Both arms got LCRT; RT is constant across arms, so the delta is chemo intensity + sequencing, not radiation

subdetails: G≥3 AEs, neoadjuvant phase: 27.59% v 8.56%, P<.001
Severe toxicity, entire course: 28.02% v 24.32%, P=.371

details: ⚠️ Locoregional failure ~6% in both arms: no local-control headroom left for RT intensification here
⚠️ Age capped at 70; per the authors, benefit-risk in older pts is unstudied
⚠️ OS not significant at 51mo (90.2% v 87.5%, P=.167); DFS/MFS gain has not translated to survival yet
🔗 vs RAPIDO / STELLAR (SCRT-based TNT) and PRODIGE-23 (FOLFIRINOX induction): this is LCRT + uninterrupted CAPOX, not tested head-to-head against either
🔍 RT dose, fractionation, and target volume not reported in source text

verdict.rationale: Phase III, prespecified DFS primary hit with 51mo f/u, but adds a third TNT variant to a paradigm RAPIDO, PRODIGE-23 and STELLAR already established. No head-to-head.
verdict.audience: Stage II/III rectal, ≥1 MRI high-risk feature (cT4, cN2, MRF+, EMVI), age ≤70

studies.significance: Locoregional failure was 6.03% v 6.19% with LCRT in both arms, so the RT question this trial answers is negative by design: intensifying chemotherapy around a fixed long-course backbone buys distant control (MFS 77.7% v 67.6%), not local. It moves the sequencing decision (consolidation CAPOX before surgery, not adjuvant after), not dose or target volume. RT dose and fractionation are not in the source text.
studies.monday_clinic: In a fit patient ≤70 with MRI high-risk stage II/III rectal cancer already headed for long-course chemoradiation, this supports moving the CAPOX to a neoadjuvant induction-plus-consolidation schedule rather than adjuvant; it does not inform short-course TNT, older or unfit pts, or a watch-and-wait organ-preservation intent.

analysis_sections.label: Design
analysis_sections.body: Multicenter randomized **phase III**, 458 pts assigned June 2017 to December 2023, median follow-up **51 months**. **Primary: DFS.** Secondary endpoints included MFS, pCR, locoregional failure, OS.

analysis_sections.label: Population & inclusion
analysis_sections.body: Stage II/III LARC, **age 18 to 70**, with at least one predefined MRI high-risk feature: **cT4a-b, cN2, threatened mesorectal fascia, or cT3c-d with EMVI**. Baseline burden was heavy: cT4 47.82%, cN2 75.98%, threatened MRF 70.96%, EMVI 54.80%.

analysis_sections.label: Regimen
analysis_sections.body: Doublet-LC TNT: **1 cycle induction CAPOX**, then LCRT with **2 cycles concurrent CAPOX**, then **3 cycles consolidation CAPOX**, then surgery. Control: LCRT with concurrent capecitabine, surgery, then **6 cycles adjuvant CAPOX** starting 4 to 8 weeks post-op.

analysis_sections.label: Radiotherapy
analysis_sections.body: **Long-course RT in both arms**, so radiation is held constant and the randomized comparison isolates chemotherapy intensity and sequencing. Dose, fractionation, and target volume are not reported in the source text.

analysis_sections.label: Results
analysis_sections.body: Primary DFS met. **Locoregional failure was equivalent (6.03% v 6.19%)** while the distant-control endpoints moved, locating the benefit outside the RT field. **3yr OS 90.2% v 87.5%, P=.167**, not significant at this follow-up.

analysis_sections.label: Safety
analysis_sections.body: Grade ≥3 AEs during the neoadjuvant phase nearly tripled (**27.59% v 8.56%, P<.001**), but across the whole treatment course the arms converged (28.02% v 24.32%, P=.371). Major postoperative complications 3.98% v 2.94%, P=.567. Roughly 87% v 90% proceeded to TME.

analysis_sections.label: Applies to
analysis_sections.body: Represents fit pts aged 70 or younger with MRI-defined high-risk stage II/III rectal cancer treated with long-course chemoradiation. Does not represent pts over 70, short-course RT schedules, or a nonoperative watch-and-wait pathway.

analysis_sections.label: Limitations
analysis_sections.body: The toxicity is front-loaded into the neoadjuvant window, where it competes with getting pts to surgery, and ~13% of the TNT arm did not reach TME. Comparators are indirect: RAPIDO, PRODIGE-23 and STELLAR used different RT schedules or induction regimens, and no randomized comparison against them exists.

analysis_sections.label: Discussion
analysis_sections.body: The trial establishes a third viable TNT backbone rather than settling which one wins. The authors name the next questions themselves: organ preservation via higher response rates, and iTNT for high-risk pMMR/MSS disease.

significance_by_specialty.radonc: RT was long-course in both arms, so nothing here changes dose, fractionation, or target volume, and locoregional failure was already floor-level at 6.03% v 6.19%. The read for an RT planner is that local control is not the limiting endpoint in high-risk LARC; the gain came from distant control (MFS 77.7% v 67.6%). RT dose and fractionation are not reported in the source text.
significance_by_specialty.medonc: The chemotherapy delta is the trial: uninterrupted CAPOX given as induction plus concurrent plus consolidation beat capecitabine-concurrent-then-adjuvant CAPOX on DFS (HR 0.674) and MFS (HR 0.655), with pCR 26.37% v 9.80%. Cost is neoadjuvant grade ≥3 AEs 27.59% v 8.56%, though whole-course severe toxicity was comparable (28.02% v 24.32%).
significance_by_specialty.surgonc: Intensified neoadjuvant chemotherapy did not degrade the operation: major postoperative complications 3.98% v 2.94% (P=.567), and roughly 87% v 90% reached TME. pCR nearly tripled to 26.37%, which raises the number of pts arriving at surgery with a complete response and sharpens the organ-preservation conversation.

open_questions: Doublet-LC TNT vs short-course RT-based TNT head-to-head
Whether higher pCR translates to durable organ preservation

studies.name: STELLAR
studies.tldr: 3yr DFS 64.5% vs 62.3% (HR 0.883) noninferior for 5x5Gy + CAPOX TNT vs long-course CRT in LARC.
details: 🔍 Phase III multicenter RCT, N=599 (TNT 302 / CRT 297), 1:1, China, accrual Aug 2015-Aug 2018
🔍 Eligibility: distal/middle-third rectal adenoca, cT3-4 and/or N+, no mets, age 18-70, ECOG 0-1
📐 RT: 25 Gy/5 fx over 1 week (TNT) vs 50 Gy/25 fx over 5 weeks with concurrent capecitabine (CRT)
🔍 TME 6-8 weeks after preop treatment in both arms; chemo load shifted preop in TNT (4 cycles CAPOX preop + 2 postop) vs 6 cycles postop in CRT

details.text: 📊 3yr outcomes, TNT vs CRT (median f/u 35.0 mo)

rows: HR 0.883, one-sided 95% CI to 1.11, P<.001 noninferiority

details: ⚠️ OS was secondary and unpowered; an 11.4-point 3yr OS gap without an MFS or LRR difference is biologically hard to explain
⚠️ DFS noninferiority margin passed on a one-sided CI upper bound of 1.11, so a real DFS decrement of up to ~11% is not excluded
⚠️ Acute G3-5 toxicity roughly doubled with TNT (26.5% vs 12.6%), all of it front-loaded before surgery
🔗 vs RAPIDO (5x5Gy + CAPOX/FOLFOX TNT): RAPIDO improved distant-metastasis-free survival but not OS or locoregional control; STELLAR is the mirror image, OS-positive with no MFS or LRR signal
🔗 vs PRODIGE 23 (induction FOLFIRINOX then long-course CRT): also DFS-positive, but keeps the 50 Gy/25 fx backbone rather than replacing it with 5x5Gy

verdict.rationale: Randomised phase III, prespecified 3yr DFS noninferiority met; aligns with RAPIDO and Polish II in supporting 5x5Gy TNT. OS gain is secondary and unpowered.
verdict.audience: cT3-4 and/or N+ distal/middle-third rectal adenocarcinoma, age 18-70, ECOG 0-1

studies.significance: The RT read is fractionation, not sequence: 25 Gy/5 fx followed by four cycles of CAPOX held 3yr DFS against 50 Gy/25 fx with concurrent capecitabine, with no difference in locoregional recurrence. That collapses 5 weeks of daily treatment into 1 week for cT3-4/N+ mid-to-low rectum. The cost is acute G3-5 toxicity at 26.5% vs 12.6%.
studies.monday_clinic: In cT3-4 and/or node-positive distal or mid-rectal adenocarcinoma headed for TME, this supports 5x5Gy plus preoperative CAPOX as an alternative to long-course chemoradiation; it does not speak to organ-preservation or watch-and-wait candidates, whose treatment goal was not what this trial tested.

primary_endpoint.name: 3-year disease-free survival
primary_endpoint.stat_detail: HR 0.883, one-sided 95% CI to 1.11, P<.001 for noninferiority

analysis_sections.label: Design
analysis_sections.body: Multicenter randomised phase III noninferiority trial, 1:1, **N=599** (TNT 302, CRT 297), enrolled August 2015 to August 2018. Median follow-up **35.0 months**.

analysis_sections.label: Population & inclusion
analysis_sections.body: Rectal adenocarcinoma of the **distal or middle third**, **cT3-4 and/or regional node-positive**, no distant metastases. Age 18-70, ECOG 0-1, no prior anticancer treatment. MRF involvement defined as tumour-to-MRF distance under 1 mm.

analysis_sections.label: Radiotherapy
analysis_sections.body: TNT arm: **25 Gy in 5 fractions over 1 week**, no concurrent chemotherapy. CRT arm: **50 Gy in 25 fractions over 5 weeks** with concurrent capecitabine. TME followed **6-8 weeks** after preoperative treatment in both arms.

analysis_sections.label: Regimen
analysis_sections.body: TNT: short-course RT then **four cycles of chemotherapy** preoperatively, plus **two** postoperative CAPOX cycles. CRT: **six** postoperative CAPOX cycles. CAPOX was oxaliplatin 130 mg/m2 day 1 with capecitabine 1,000 mg/m2 twice daily days 1-14.

analysis_sections.label: Endpoints
analysis_sections.body: **Primary: 3-year disease-free survival**, tested for noninferiority. Secondary included metastasis-free survival, locoregional recurrence, overall survival, compliance and toxicity.

analysis_sections.label: Results
analysis_sections.body: Noninferiority met. **3yr OS favoured TNT, 86.5% v 75.1% (P=.033)**, with **no significant difference in MFS or locoregional recurrence**. Treatment effects on DFS and OS were similar across prognostic factor subgroups.

analysis_sections.label: Safety
analysis_sections.body: Acute **grade III-V toxicity during preoperative treatment was 26.5% with TNT versus 12.6% with CRT (P<.001)**, roughly double. The source reports no late-toxicity comparison.

analysis_sections.label: vs leading data
analysis_sections.body: RAPIDO used the same **5x5Gy plus consolidation chemotherapy** backbone and improved distant-metastasis-free survival without an OS or locoregional-control gain. STELLAR shows the inverse pattern, an OS separation with flat MFS and LRR.

analysis_sections.label: Applies to
analysis_sections.body: Represents cT3-4 and/or node-positive distal and mid-rectal adenocarcinoma in pts aged 18-70 with ECOG 0-1 proceeding to TME. Does not represent upper-third tumours, pts over 70, cT1-2 N0 disease, or nonoperative organ-preservation strategies.

analysis_sections.label: Limitations
analysis_sections.body: The **OS gain is a secondary endpoint with no supporting MFS or locoregional signal**, so the mechanism is unexplained and the result may be a chance finding. Adjuvant chemotherapy completion, the stated rationale for moving chemo preoperatively, is not quantified in the source text. Median follow-up of 35.0 months is short for a 3-year DFS trial.

significance_by_specialty.radonc: Fractionation is the decision: 25 Gy/5 fx with no concurrent agent matched 50 Gy/25 fx plus capecitabine on 3yr DFS, with no difference in locoregional recurrence. For cT3-4/N+ mid-to-low rectum, that is 5 weeks of daily treatment compressed into 1, at the cost of 26.5% versus 12.6% acute G3-5 toxicity.
significance_by_specialty.medonc: Chemotherapy sequence, not dose, is what moved: four preoperative cycles plus two postoperative in TNT versus six postoperative in CRT, built on the premise that only about 50% of pts finish adjuvant chemotherapy after CRT. The 3yr OS gap (86.5% v 75.1%, P=.033) came without an MFS difference, so the systemic mechanism is unproven.
significance_by_specialty.surgonc: TME timing was unchanged, 6-8 weeks after preoperative treatment in both arms, so short-course RT plus 4 cycles of chemotherapy does not push the operation later than long-course chemoradiation does. Locoregional recurrence did not differ, though the source reports no pCR, R0 or sphincter-preservation rates to gauge resection difficulty.

open_questions: Is the 3yr OS separation real without an MFS or LRR difference?
Late toxicity and anorectal function after 5x5Gy TNT versus long-course CRT
Does 5x5Gy TNT support organ preservation and watch-and-wait?

papers.title: Total Neoadjuvant Therapy With Long-Course Radiotherapy Versus Chemoradiotherapy in High-Risk Locally Advanced Rectal Cancer (TNTCRT): A Multicenter, Randomized, Phase III Trial
papers.abstract: PURPOSE High-risk locally advanced rectal cancer (LARC) carries a substantial risk of distant recurrence, which limits disease-free survival (DFS). We compared total neoadjuvant therapy (TNT) integrating long-course radiotherapy (LCRT) with uninterrupted doublet chemotherapy (doublet-LC TNT) versus conventional neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy (nCRT). METHODS In this multicenter, randomized, phase III trial, patients with stage II/III LARC and at least 1 high-risk feature (cT4a-b, cN2, mesorectal fascia involvement, or cT3c-d with extramural vascular invasion) were enrolled. Patients were assigned to doublet-LC TNT (induction, concurrent, and consolidation capecitabine plus oxaliplatin with LCRT) before surgery or nCRT (capecitabine with LCRT) followed by surgery and adjuvant chemotherapy. The primary end point was DFS (ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT03177382 ). RESULTS Between June 6, 2017, and December 27, 2023, 458 patients were randomly assigned to doublet-LC TNT (n = 232) or nCRT (n = 226). At a median follow-up of 51 months, doublet-LC TNT improved 3-year DFS (74.8% v 66.0%; hazard ratio [HR], 0.674 [95% CI, 0.489 to 0.929]; P = .016). Metastasis-free survival (MFS; 77.7% v 67.6%; HR, 0.655 [95% CI, 0.469 to 0.915]) and pathologic complete response rates (pCR; 26.37% v 9.80%; P < .001) were higher with doublet-LC TNT, whereas locoregional failure remained low and comparable (6.03% v 6.19%; P = .943). Although grade ≥3 adverse events during the neoadjuvant phase were more frequent with doublet-LC TNT (27.59% v 8.56%; P < .001), severe toxicities during the entire treatment course (28.02% v 24.32%; P = .371) and major postoperative complications (3.98% v 2.94%; P = .567) were comparable. CONCLUSION Compared with conventional nCRT, doublet-LC TNT improved DFS, MFS, and pCR rates with manageable toxicity. These findings support this intensified, doublet-based regimen as a standard option within the modern TNT paradigm. Further comparative studies are warranted to evaluate these results against other short-course radiotherapy‑based or nondoublet-concurrent TNT regimens.

papers.title: Multicenter, Randomized, Phase III Trial of Short-Term Radiotherapy Plus Chemotherapy Versus Long-Term Chemoradiotherapy in Locally Advanced Rectal Cancer (STELLAR)
papers.abstract: PURPOSE To ascertain if preoperative short-term radiotherapy followed by chemotherapy is not inferior to a standard schedule of long-term chemoradiotherapy in patients with locally advanced rectal cancer. MATERIALS AND METHODS Patients with distal or middle-third, clinical primary tumor stage 3-4 and/or regional lymph node–positive rectal cancer were randomly assigned (1:1) to short-term radiotherapy (25 Gy in five fractions over 1 week) followed by four cycles of chemotherapy (total neoadjuvant therapy [TNT]) or chemoradiotherapy (50 Gy in 25 fractions over 5 weeks, concurrently with capecitabine [chemoradiotherapy; CRT]). Total mesorectal excision was undertaken 6-8 weeks after preoperative treatment, with two additional cycles of CAPOX (intravenous oxaliplatin [130 mg/m 2 , once a day] on day 1 and capecitabine [1,000 mg/m 2 , twice a day] from days 1 to 14) in the TNT group and six cycles of CAPOX in the CRT group. The primary end point was 3-year disease-free survival (DFS). RESULTS Between August 2015 and August 2018, a total of 599 patients were randomly assigned to receive TNT (n = 302) or CRT (n = 297). At a median follow-up of 35.0 months, 3-year DFS was 64.5% and 62.3% in TNT and CRT groups, respectively (hazard ratio, 0.883; one-sided 95% CI, not applicable to 1.11; P < .001 for noninferiority). There was no significant difference in metastasis-free survival or locoregional recurrence, but the TNT group had better 3-year overall survival than the CRT group (86.5% v 75.1%; P = .033). Treatment effects on DFS and overall survival were similar regardless of prognostic factors. The prevalence of acute grade III-V toxicities during preoperative treatment was 26.5% in the TNT group versus 12.6% in the CRT group ( P < .001). CONCLUSION Short-term radiotherapy with preoperative chemotherapy followed by surgery was efficacious with acceptable toxicity and could be used as an alternative to CRT for locally advanced rectal cancer.
